title: Monotone Increasing Digits
summary: Determine the greatest integer not exceeding n that possesses digits in non-decreasing order, where each adjacent pair of digits x and y fulfills x <= y.
statement: Determine the greatest integer not exceeding n that possesses digits in non-decreasing order, where each adjacent pair of digits x and y fulfills x <= y.
constraints: Return the greatest integer no larger than n whose digits are nondecreasing left to right.
hints: Repairing a violation may create another violation to its left.
Scan right-to-left, decrement offending predecessors, then maximize the suffix with nines.
Record the earliest repaired suffix boundary and replace every later digit by nine.
The prefix is the largest feasible monotone prefix; all nines make its suffix maximal without exceeding n.
editorial: The prefix is the largest feasible monotone prefix; all nines make its suffix maximal without exceeding n.

tests.explanation: Decreasing the first digit and filling the suffix gives 9.
The rightmost violation propagates left, producing 299.
